content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge marks UNDERDETERMINED on the basis that both the challenger's covenant-origin analogy and the sentence's own stated source are supported, so it treats the verse as carrying two senses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open: (1) the covenant-origin analogy and the stated source are two senses of Matthew 1:20, so UNDERDETERMINED is forbidden; (2) the analogy is external support, so the verse carries one sense and the clause does not apply.","why":"The judge calls the item UNDERDETERMINED while identifying two supported readings of the same verse, which K-S2 says are not open and both stand."}
